governance_rules.name: Small Incremental Autonomous Operations Required
governance_rules.description:
ALL orchestrators MUST work in small, meaningful increments to prevent
token limit errors and server failures (HTTP 502).

Large monolithic operations that exceed token context windows cause
catastrophic failures. Orchestrators MUST operate autonomously without
manual intervention between increments.
validation: Operations split into <500 line increments per execution
Each increment is independently executable
State persisted between increments (continuation support)
Token usage monitored and capped at 80% of limit
Autonomous mode enabled by default (no user prompts mid-execution)

pass: Phase 1: Process 50 files → Phase 2: Process next 50 files (incremental)
Orchestrator completes Phase 1 autonomously → Auto-proceeds to Phase 2
Token usage 75% → Checkpoint state → Continue in next turn
fail: Process all 1000 files in single execution (causes 502 error)
Orchestrator pauses mid-execution waiting for user approval
No state persistence between phases (restart from scratch)

governance_rules.error_reference: Server error 502 (request ID: c43bcffb-60ff-4d8c-ae4c-0c56e1c679cd) - Token limit exceeded
governance_rules.rationale:
Incremental execution prevents:
1. Token limit errors (HTTP 502, context overflow)
2. Loss of work (operation fails halfway, no state saved)
3. Manual intervention burden (user must approve every step)
4. Timeout failures (operation takes too long)
5. Memory exhaustion (processing too much data at once)

governance_rules.description:
ALL public Python modules, classes, functions, and methods MUST have

Docstrings explain WHY code exists and HOW to use it, not WHAT it does
(code explains that).
validation: All public modules must have module docstrings
All public classes must have class docstrings
All public functions/methods must have docstrings with Args/Returns/Raises
Private functions (starting with _) are exempt but encouraged
Docstrings must follow Google style format

governance_rules.name: Explicit Error Handling with Custom Exceptions
governance_rules.description:
ALL error conditions MUST be handled explicitly with custom exception
classes.

Bare except blocks and generic Exception catching are PROHIBITED.
CORTEX must fail fast with clear error messages, not hide failures.
validation: No bare except clauses (must specify exception type)
No catching generic Exception without re-raising
Custom exception classes for domain-specific errors
All exceptions must have descriptive messages

governance_rules.name: SOLID Principles Enforcement
governance_rules.description:
ALL Python classes and modules MUST follow SOLID principles.

Single Responsibility, Open/Closed, Liskov Substitution, Interface
Segregation, Dependency Inversion.
validation: Single Responsibility - Class has one reason to change
Open/Closed - Extend behavior via inheritance/composition, not modification
Liskov Substitution - Subclasses must be substitutable for base classes
Interface Segregation - Many specific interfaces > one general interface
Dependency Inversion - Depend on abstractions (protocols), not concrete classes

governance_rules.name: Import Organization (PEP 8)
governance_rules.description:
ALL Python imports MUST be organized in 3 groups: stdlib, third-party,

Each group separated by blank line, sorted alphabetically.
validation: Imports grouped in 3 sections (stdlib, third-party, local)
Each section sorted alphabetically
Blank line between sections
No wildcard imports (from x import *)
Absolute imports preferred over relative

governance_rules.name: Black Code Formatting

governance_rules.name: YAML-First Design Mandatory
governance_rules.description:
ALL orchestrators, plans, and implementations MUST follow YAML-first

Markdown plan files (*-PLAN.md, *-plan.md) are PROHIBITED. All planning
and tracking must use YAML files (00-TODO-CONTINUITY-TRACKER.yaml,
features-summary.yaml, etc.).

Exceptions:

- README.md files for quick-start guides
- CONTINUATION-PROMPT.md (auto-generated)

VIOLATION EXAMPLES:
- feat04-core-orchestration-PLAN.md (should be in tracker YAML)
- intelligence-layer-design.md in docs/planning/ (should be YAML or deleted)
validation: No *-PLAN.md or *-plan.md files (use YAML tracker)
No *-design.md files in planning/ (use architecture/ or YAML)
No implementation-*.md files (should be YAML configs)

validation.Exception: architecture/ folder can have .md docs (optional, prefer YAML)

audit_logging.message_template: Blocked {file_path}: YAML-first violation - use YAML for plans/configs

git_hook_enforcement.error_message:
❌ YAML-FIRST VIOLATION DETECTED

The following files violate YAML-first principle:
{violated_files}

✅ CORRECT APPROACH:
- Use 00-TODO-CONTINUITY-TRACKER.yaml for task tracking
- Use YAML configs for orchestrator rules/settings
- Architecture docs (optional) go in cortex-brain/documents/architecture/

governance_rules.rationale:
YAML-first prevents:
1. Markdown bloat (verbose text files that duplicate tracker data)
2. Parser ambiguity (Markdown requires LLM parsing, YAML is machine-readable)
3. Inconsistent planning (some use MD, some use YAML)
4. Workspace clutter (unnecessary planning documents)
5. Feature drift (implementation diverges from plan when not YAML-driven)

Benefits of YAML-first:
1. Machine-readable (no LLM parsing needed)
2. Validation possible (JSON schema, linters)
3. Consistent structure (all plans follow same format)
4. Direct execution (YAML → Python execution without translation)
5. Token efficiency (compact, no natural language bloat)

Markdown is ONLY acceptable for:

STRICTLY FORBIDDEN in cortex-brain/:
- cortex-brain/tier0/ → YAML only (governance rules)
- cortex-brain/tier1/ → YAML/JSON only (tracking, acceptance criteria)
- cortex-brain/tier2/ → YAML only (engineering standards)
- cortex-brain/tier3/ → YAML only (domain patterns)
- cortex-brain/config/ → YAML only
- cortex-brain/manifests/ → YAML only

All knowledge files MUST be machine-readable. No markdown in brain.
validation: Orchestrator outputs use YAML/JSON/Python, not markdown
Plans stored in YAML (00-TODO-CONTINUITY-TRACKER.yaml pattern)
Reports use YAML structure (not *-report.md)

governance_rules.name: Kebab-Case File Naming with 20-Character Limit
governance_rules.description:
ALL file names MUST follow kebab-case format (lowercase, hyphen-separated)
with a maximum of 20 characters EXCLUDING the file extension.

This rule is FINAL and SUPERSEDES any conflicting naming conventions
elsewhere in the codebase or documentation.

Format: `{name}.{ext}` where:
- `name` = 1-20 lowercase alphanumeric characters with hyphens
- Hyphens cannot be leading, trailing, or consecutive
- Extension is NOT counted in the 20-character limit

EXCEPTIONS (grandfathered):
- Python files with underscores in src/ (Python module convention)
- __init__.py, __main__.py, conftest.py (Python special files)
- LICENSE, README.md, Makefile (standard project files)
- .gitignore, .env, .editorconfig (dotfiles)
validation: File name (excluding extension) <= 20 characters
No uppercase characters in file name
No underscores in file name (except Python src/ files)
No spaces or special characters
No consecutive hyphens (--)
No leading or trailing hyphens

python_modules.description: Python files in src/ may use underscores per PEP 8

supersedes.description: This rule is FINAL and overrides any conflicting rules

migration_guidance.description: Existing files violating this rule should be renamed

governance_rules.rationale:
Kebab-case with length limits ensures:
1. Cross-platform compatibility (Windows, macOS, Linux)
2. URL-safe file names (no encoding needed)
3. Readable file names (hyphens more readable than underscores)
4. Consistent naming across entire codebase
5. Predictable file discovery and sorting
6. Git-friendly (avoids case-sensitivity issues)
7. Terminal-friendly (no quoting needed)
8. 20-char limit prevents unwieldy names while allowing descriptive names

governance_rules.name: File Type-Specific Validation Required Before Commit
governance_rules.description:
Modified files MUST pass file-type-specific validation before state
changes (git commit, plan completion, orchestrator finish).

This is a PRE-COMMIT quality gate, NOT a TDD cycle requirement.
Validation happens once at completion, not during development iterations.

Validation per file type:
- .html → HTML5 syntax (html5lib) + WCAG AA compliance (zero tolerance)
- .yaml → Schema validation + YAML syntax (already enforced by OE-002)
- .py → pytest + test coverage (handled by TDD-Master via CORE-019)
- .json → JSON syntax validation
- .css → CSS syntax validation (optional)

CRITICAL: HTML files MUST NOT be left in broken states. Any HTML
modification by any orchestrator or GitHub Copilot MUST result in
valid HTML5 with zero parse errors.

html_files: Parse with html5lib (TreeBuilder with strict mode)
No unclosed tags, no malformed attributes
WCAG AA compliance (contrast ratios, semantic HTML, ARIA)
python_files: All tests pass (TDD-Master ensures this via CORE-019)
No validation needed at pre-commit (already tested)
json_files: Schema validation if JSON schema exists

applies_to: Manual HTML edits by GitHub Copilot

on_html_validation_failure.message:
❌ HTML VALIDATION FAILED

Modified HTML file(s) contain syntax errors or WCAG violations.
All HTML must be valid HTML5 with zero parse errors.

Run validator manually:
  python -m src.orchestrators.html_view.validators.html_validator <file.html>

Or fix via HTMLViewOrchestrator:
  python -m src.main "fix visual issues in <file.html>"

pass: Modified docs/features/index.html → html5lib validates → ✓ commit allowed
Fixed docs/orchestrators/planning.html → WCAG AA compliant → ✓ commit allowed
Updated config.yaml → schema valid → ✓ commit allowed (OE-002)
fail: Modified index.html with unclosed <div> → ❌ blocked (HTML5 error)
Added feature.html with contrast ratio 2.5:1 → ❌ blocked (WCAG AA requires 4.5:1)

integration_points: HTMLViewOrchestrator Phase 5 (VALIDATION) runs same checks during development
Pre-commit hook (scripts/pre-commit) enforces at commit time
GitHub Copilot edits HTML → pre-commit catches issues before merge
TDD-Master does NOT validate HTML (separation of concerns)
performance: Validation only on modified files (not entire codebase)
WCAG validation: ~200ms per file (contrast checks, semantic analysis)
Total overhead: <1 second for typical commits (1-5 HTML files)
governance_rules.rationale:
Zero-tolerance HTML validation prevents:
1. Broken HTML merged into main branch (blocks GitHubPages deployment)
2. WCAG AA violations (accessibility compliance failures)
3. Browser rendering issues (parse errors cause layout breaks)
4. Developer confusion (debug time wasted on malformed HTML)
5. Accumulated technical debt (broken HTML compounds over time)

This rule addresses the observed pattern of TDD-Master and other
orchestrators leaving HTML in broken states. By validating at the
quality gate layer (pre-commit), we catch issues before they pollute
the repository.

Architectural rationale:
- HTML validation is NOT a TDD concern (HTML is declarative, not testable code)
- Separation of concerns: HTMLViewOrchestrator handles HTML, TDD-Master handles code
- Pre-commit hooks are the correct architectural layer for cross-cutting quality checks
- This approach is extensible (easy to add CSS linting, Markdown validation, etc.)

governance_rules.name: All MCP Tools MUST Use @mcp_tool Decorator
governance_rules.description:
ALL tools in src/mcp/*_tools.py MUST use the @mcp_tool decorator for
automatic registration. Manual registration is FORBIDDEN.

This prevents registration drift where tools exist but aren't exposed
via MCP, causing silent failures in capability discovery.

The decorator provides:
- Automatic registration at import time (no manual registry calls)
- Consistent metadata structure (name, description, parameters, returns)
- JSON Schema validation for parameters
- Category-based grouping
- Versioning and audit trails
validation: All functions in src/mcp/*_tools.py have @mcp_tool decorator
Decorator precedes function definition immediately (no blank lines)
Decorator includes: name, description, category, parameters
Parameter definitions include: type, required, description
Returns definition specifies output schema

static_analysis: AST parsing: Find function definitions in *_tools.py without decorator
Grep pattern: Functions matching 'def (.*?)\(' without '@mcp_tool' above
Import check: Verify decorator imported from src.mcp.mcp_decorator
runtime_check: Compare: Functions in tool modules vs. decorated tool registry
Alert: If function count > decorated count (drift detected)

on_undecorated_tool.message:
❌ MCP TOOL DECORATOR VIOLATION (CORE-024)

Found function(s) in src/mcp/*_tools.py without @mcp_tool decorator.
This causes registration drift - tool exists but not exposed via MCP.

Add decorator:
  from src.mcp.mcp_decorator import mcp_tool
  
  @mcp_tool(
      name="cortex_<function_name>",
      description="Tool description",
      category="<audit|governance|planning|etc>",
      parameters={...},
      returns={...}
  )
  def your_function(...):
      pass

See: cortex-brain/tier2/mcp-tool-creation-protocol.md
on_undecorated_tool.bypass: git commit --no-verify (EMERGENCY ONLY - creates audit alert)

fail:
# ❌ WRONG: Manual registration (bypasses decorator)
def audit_query(db_path: str):
    pass

# Manual registry.register() call - FORBIDDEN
# ❌ WRONG: Missing decorator

    pass  # Will NOT be exposed via MCP

integration_points: CapabilityRegistry auto-discovers decorated tools at startup
Pre-commit hook blocks undecorated tools before merge
MCP server lists all decorated tools via /tools/list
Audit logs record tool registrations with decorator metadata

cross_repo_support.cortex_discovery:
CORTEX scans sys.modules for cortex_mcp_protocol presence.
If found, imports user's decorated tools and merges into registry.

performance: Decorator overhead: <1ms per tool (executed once at import)
Pre-commit check: ~50ms (AST parsing of 7 tool modules)
Runtime discovery: ~100ms (imports all tool modules once)
governance_rules.rationale:
Prevents registration drift - the #1 failure mode in MCP exposure:

WITHOUT decorator:
1. Developer creates tool function
2. Forgets manual registry.register() call
3. Code merges, tests pass (no detection)
4. Tool exists but not discoverable via MCP
5. Silent failure - users can't find tool
6. Remediation required (audit finds drift 3 days later)

WITH decorator:
1. Developer creates tool function
2. Pre-commit hook detects missing decorator → blocks commit
3. Developer adds decorator
4. Import triggers auto-registration (no manual call)
5. Tool immediately discoverable via MCP
6. Zero drift possible

Decorator pattern is PROACTIVE (prevents wrong code) vs. governance
validation which is REACTIVE (detects wrong code after merge).

Multi-layer defense:
- Layer 1: SKULL rule (this) - blocks at commit time
- Layer 2: Template scaffolder (AC-MCP-PROTOCOL-002) - generates correct code
- Layer 3: Cross-repo plugin (AC-MCP-PROTOCOL-003) - portable protocol
- Layer 4: Documentation - developer guidance
